title: Herrgott Road rehabilitation contract increase approved
subtitle: Council also approved 2023 financial results and a Habitat for Humanity water infrastructure relocation agreement in Kitchener.
overview: At a short special meeting, Regional Council increased the contract and project budget for the Regional Road 10 (Herrgott Road) rehabilitation. The contract with Capital Paving Inc. rose by $666,719.47, to a total of $4,187,732.67 plus taxes, and the project budget rose by $678,700 {{vote:m1}}. The road is a regional route near St. Clements, so the funding allows the work to continue.
Council also approved the preliminary 2023 financial results so the Region's 2023 audited financial statements can be prepared, and applied the Surplus Allocation Policy to those results {{vote:m2}}.

Council then suspended its procedural rules to take up an item not listed in the meeting notice {{vote:m3}}. It authorized an agreement with Habitat for Humanity Waterloo Region Inc. to relocate critical Regional water infrastructure at 100 St George St, Kitchener {{vote:m4}}. The item came from the Planning and Works Committee earlier that day and was brought forward to speed it up.

decisions.detail: Council increased the Capital Paving Inc. contract by $666,719.47 to $4,187,732.67 plus taxes and raised the Project #05758 budget by $678,700.
Council approved the preliminary 2023 financial results for preparing the audited statements and applied the Surplus Allocation Policy.
Council suspended the procedural by-law rules to consider a matter not set out in the notice calling the special meeting.

Council approved an agreement with Habitat for Humanity Waterloo Region Inc. to relocate critical Regional water infrastructure at 100 St George St, Kitchener, and authorized the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services to sign it.

debate: Discussion was minimal; the Herrgott Road item, the committee summary and the Habitat for Humanity agreement each went to a vote with little or no debate.

One councillor commented, while acknowledging it was editorial, that Council had just approved a budget increase after earlier turning down a $50,000 request to plant trees that had already been planted. The Chair noted this was editorializing, and no one else spoke on it.
On the suspension of rules, the Chair clarified that it applied to this particular matter at this time and that the required two-thirds threshold had been met.
